messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

**To:** Engineering leadership
**From:** Héctor Quezada
**Re:** Giving Q4 to technical debt

I want the platform team off the roadmap for one quarter. Four engineers, twelve weeks, spent on debt and nothing else.

The argument here is arithmetic, not taste. Our median PR now sits open 4.1 days before it merges; a year ago that number was 1.6. CI takes 47 minutes and fails at random on roughly one run in six, so most engineers push twice to earn one green build. Of the 31 production incidents we logged last quarter, 19 came out of three services that still share a database schema nobody owns. That is the bill we already pay, and it grows every quarter we defer it.

What the twelve weeks go toward, in order: separate the shared schema so each service owns its migrations; get CI under 15 minutes by parallelizing the integration suite and deleting the roughly 200 tests that assert nothing; retire the v1 API, which carries 0.3% of traffic while constraining every routing change we make.

None of this is free. Four features slip, and I would rather choose which four in October than watch them slip anyway in March. What we've been doing instead, a debt sprint every few months, hasn't worked, because the work crosses service boundaries and won't fit in two weeks.

I'll report against those three numbers every two weeks. If none of them has moved by week six, cancel the quarter and put the team back on the roadmap.

Swap in your own metrics before this goes out. The argument only works if the numbers are real.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

Where the twelve weeks go, in order: split the shared schema so every service owns its own migrations; cut CI below 15 minutes by parallelizing the integration suite and deleting the ~200 tests that assert nothing; kill the v1 API, which carries 0.3% of traffic and blocks every routing change we want to make.

There is a cost. Four features slip. I would rather pick which four in October than watch them slip anyway in March. The alternative we've been running, a debt sprint every few months, has failed, because this work crosses service boundaries and doesn't fit in two weeks.
